paragraphs.text: Or, Even Johanan; he among the rest, and above the rest. Ille huic negotio non interfuit modo, sed etiam praefuit.
paragraphs.anchor: Then all the captains of the forces and Johanan.

paragraphs.text: Brother, belike, to that Azariah, {Jer 43:2} a noble pair of brethren in evil.
paragraphs.anchor: And Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah.

paragraphs.text: Who follow their rulers; as in a beast the whole body followeth the head.
paragraphs.anchor: And all the people.

paragraphs.text: They came as clients use to do for counsel.
paragraphs.anchor: Drew near.

paragraphs.text: Here they seem to humble themselves before Jeremiah the prophet; which, because King Zedekiah did not, he came to ruin. {2Ch 36:12}
paragraphs.anchor: Let, we beseech thee, our supplication be accepted before thee.

paragraphs.text: Good words may be found even in a hellish mouth sometimes. Who would think but these men had spoken what they did unfeignedly, and from their very hearts? whenas it soon after appeared that all was no better than deep dissimulation. They had made their conclusion beforehand to go down to Egypt, only in a pretence of piety, and for greater credit, they would have had God’s approbation; which, since they cannot, they will go on with their design however, fall back, fall edge. O most hateful hypocrisy! O contumacy worthy of all men’s execration!
paragraphs.anchor: And pray for us unto the Lord thy God.

paragraphs.text: But they had set themselves in the way to Egypt before they came with this request to the prophet: why went they else to Goruth Chimham, the road toward Egypt? {Jer 41:17} why were they also so peremptory, when they knew God’s mind to the contrary? {Jer 43:7}
paragraphs.anchor: That the Lord thy God may show us the way.

paragraphs.text: Good words all along; but those, we say, are light cheap: Quid vero verba quaero, facta cum videam? They were as forward to speak fair, as their ancestors were in the wilderness; but oh that there were a heart in this people, saith God, to do as they have said!
paragraphs.anchor: And the thing that we may do.

paragraphs.text: The wisdom from above is persuasible, easy to be entreated, {Jas 3:18} and good men are ready to every good work. {Tit 3:1} Jeremiah hoped they might speak their whole hearts, and promiseth to do his best for them, both by praying and prophesying.
paragraphs.anchor: I have heard you; behold, I will pray.

paragraphs.text: Sic veteres nihil ex se vel potuerunt, vel protulerunt. The prophets spake as they were inspired by the Spirit of truth. Christ spake nothing but what was consonant to the Holy Scriptures. The apostles delivered to the churches what they had received of the Lord. {1Co 11:23} Polycarp told the churches that he delivered nothing to them but what he had received of the apostles. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Whatsoever thing the Lord shall answer you, I will declare.

paragraphs.text: {a} Irenaeus, lib. iii.; Eccles. Hist., lib. iv. cap. 14.
Did these men know what it was so solemnly to swear a thing? Or were they stark atheists, thus to promise that with an oath which they never meant to perform?
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord be a true and faithful witness between us.

paragraphs.text: “ At sperate Deum memorem fandi atque nefandi. ”
Their king, Zedekiah, paid dearly for his perjury to God and men.

i.e., Whether it please us or cross us. Veniat, veniat verbum Domini: et submittemus ei, sexcenta si nobis essent colla, said a good man once - that is, Let God’s Word come to us once and he shall be obeyed, whatever come of it. These in the text seem to say as much, but they say it only; neither was it much to be liked that they were so free of their promises, and all in their own strength, without any condition of help from heaven: as if the matter had been wholly in their own hands, and they had free will to whatsoever good purpose or practice.
paragraphs.anchor: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil

paragraphs.text: “ O caecas mentes hominum! ”
“O the blind mind of men”
Yes, as far as a few good words will go.
paragraphs.anchor: We will obey the voice of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: “ Pollicitis dives quilibet esse potest. ” - Ovid.

So long God held his holy prophet in request; and so he doth still his best servants many times, thereby tying, as it were, the sacrifice to the horns of the altar. How impatient those wretched roysters were of such a delay, we may well imagine (the Chinese use to whip their gods when they will not hear and help them forthwith); but God held them off as unworthy of any answer, and seemed by his silence to say unto them, as in Eze 20:3, "Are ye come to inquire of me? As I live, saith the Lord, I will not be inquired of by you."
paragraphs.anchor: And it came to pass that after ten days.

paragraphs.text: For the Word of God belongeth to all of all sorts; and as the smaller fish bite first, so the poor are evangelized {Mat 11:5} when the richer stand off.
paragraphs.anchor: And all the people, from the least unto the greatest.

paragraphs.text: Heb., To make your supplication fall in his presence. This I have not ceased to do ever since, but had no answer till now; and it may be that now you may the better regard it. Cito data eito vilescunt. Soon given, soon worthless.
paragraphs.anchor: Unto whom ye sent me to present your supplication.

paragraphs.text: Promittitur felicitatio; parabola ab architectura et agricultura desumpta. God promiseth to bless and settle them by a twofold similitude, used also by the apostle, {1Co 3:9} "Ye are God’s husbandry, ye are God’s building." See Jer 24:6.
paragraphs.anchor: Then will I build you.

paragraphs.text: A term taken from men, {Gen 6:6} though repentance in men is a change of the will; but repentance in God is only the willing of a change, mutatio rei, non Dei. See Jer 18:8.
paragraphs.anchor: For I repent me of the evil.

paragraphs.text: See on Jer 41:18.
paragraphs.anchor: Fear not the king of Babylon.

paragraphs.text: Not only to protect you from the Babylonian, but also to incline his heart to clemency toward you. {Jer 42:12}
paragraphs.anchor: For I am with you to save you.

paragraphs.text: Tender mercies, such as proceed from the heart, and of a parent, nay, a mother. This was more than all the rest.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will shew mercies unto you.

paragraphs.text: Because more barren than Egypt, and besides beset with many and mighty enemies
paragraphs.anchor: But if ye say, We will not dwell in this land.

paragraphs.text: Which you ought to do, whatever come of it, since rebellion is as witchcraft. {1Sa 15:22-23}
paragraphs.anchor: Neither obey the voice of the Lord your God.

paragraphs.text: Infamous for idolatry, luxury, and the oppression of your ancestors there, besides God’s express prohibition and {Deu 17:16} commination of it, as the last and greatest plague. "The Lord shall bring thee unto Egypt." {Deu 28:68}
paragraphs.anchor: Saying, No; but we will go into the land of Egypt.

paragraphs.text: The prophet now, by their looks, or some other way, perceived their purpose so to do, whatever they had promised. {Jer 42:5-6}
paragraphs.anchor: And there will we dwell.

paragraphs.text: As now I see ye do, and shall therefore tell you what to trust unto; with the froward God will wrestle. {Psa 18:26}
paragraphs.anchor: If ye wholly set your faces.

paragraphs.text: Categorice intonat propheta. God hath long hands; neither can wicked men anywhere live out of the reach of his rod.
paragraphs.anchor: Then it shall come to pass, that the sword which ye feared shall overtake you there.

paragraphs.text: Egypt was very fertile, the granary of the world, and yet God could cause a famine there; he hath treasures of plagues for sinners, and can never be exhausted.
paragraphs.anchor: And the famine whereof ye were afraid.

paragraphs.text: Three threats, answerable to those three promises, {Jer 42:10-12} in case of their obedience.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence.

paragraphs.text: {a} scil., Like scalding lead or burning bell-metal, {b} which runneth fiercely, spreadeth far, and burneth extremely.
paragraphs.anchor: As mine anger and my fury hath been poured forth

paragraphs.text: Out of which fire I have late pulled you as a brand; the smell thereof is yet upon your clothes, as it were: Cavete. Beware.
paragraphs.anchor: Upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: {a} Metaph. a metallis.
{b} The substance of which bells are made; an alloy of copper and tin, the tin being in larger proportion than in ordinary bronze.

Be ruled, or you will rue it when you have learned their evil manners, and shall perish in their punishments. It is better for you to be in cold irons at Babylon than to serve idols in Egypt at never so much liberty. Your fathers brought a golden calf thence; Jeroboam brought two.
paragraphs.anchor: Go ye not into Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Ye seduced in your souls or in your minds. The Vulgate hath it, You deceived your souls, and not God, by playing fast and loose with him, by dealing with him ac si puer esset, scurra, vel morio, and if he sould be a boy, a baffoon or an idiot.
paragraphs.anchor: For ye dissembled in your hearts.

paragraphs.text: Nay, you take a clean contrary course, as if ye would despitefully spit in the face of Heaven, and wrestle a fall with the Almighty.
paragraphs.anchor: But ye have not obeyed the voice of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: In running from death ye shall but run to it, as Jonah did.
paragraphs.anchor: Now, therefore, know certainly that ye shall die.

paragraphs.text: “ Quo fugis, Encelade? quaseunque accesseris orss,
Sub Iove semper eris. ”
